Task 0's reversed duplicate exam V73-261204-4409 therefore leaves Ivy a new patient in the rule words and in the compute alike. K2: the fitting ladders carry the values the record can take: exam visit = routine exam with a specialty fitting line / with a standard fitting line / without a fitting line (0.00); both out-of-network claim rules = specialty fitting line / standard fitting line / no fitting line (0.00); the baselines stay the standard sentences (every exam-visit line at exam_fee_private; a fitting out of network at oon_exam_reimbursement). (1) The assembly sentences of the contact-lens order and the stand-alone fitting are generic: every discount part that applies is added into one rate taken once off the retail charge, every fitting allowance that applies is added into one combined fitting allowance, and the fitting share is taken as the fitting sentences state; no factor-only quantity is named there. (4) The exam visit states its out-of-network fitting amount (oon_exam_reimbursement, whatever the kind) in its own standard sentence, also in the computation baseline; fitting_type_fee now owns only the participating schedule. Each selection sentence now states the compute's precedence (independent practice, then retail chain, then the not-eligible lines; specialty before standard for fittings); the exam visit takes the fitting only on a claim without contact lenses; the stand-alone fitting settles nothing (0.00) when the claim it looks at carries a routine exam or contact-lens line; the contact-lens order counts open spectacle-lens or frame lines of its own claim as glasses (the eyeglasses order of the same claim settled first), so a mixed claim has one outcome in either decision order. The four agent tools now record only the lines their rule owns (the member tools still record every line of the new out-of-network claim); every task claim carries the lines of one rule only, so replay is unchanged. (6) The stand-alone fitting states the not-covered case first (participating: discounted charge; out of network: nothing reimbursed) and then the covered out-of-network reimbursement, as the compute now applies them. (7) Every eligibility sentence and binder ladder says the latest binder payment is read (its return, amount and date), as the compute reads it. J2: the frequency sentences count from the latest paid or reimbursed service of the kind; a reversal frees the benefit only when it reverses the one paid service on that latest date (several on that date leave it blocked, whatever the row order); this and the current-enrollment scope are declared as a scoped overwrite naming the five sibling rules. J3 (re-stated in round 8 for K4): contacts-in-lieu reads, for each kind of the other side (spectacle lenses, frames, contact lenses), the latest paid or reimbursed service with the reversal rule of the frequency sentence, and counts it when it is dated in the same benefit period as the service settled, a benefit period starting each year on benefit_period_start_mmdd; a latest service in another benefit period counts nothing; declared as a scoped overwrite naming the five sibling rules. J10: the fitting line counts in the contact-lens part of the in-lieu comparison and follows the contact-lens line; a fitting on a claim without contact lenses is reimbursed on its own. J4: the location split of the child copay is gone; one pediatric band remains as a three-tier ladder with the out-of-network tier (no copay out of network) on agent rules that now settle out-of-network lines. J5: no new-wearer discount on contact lenses; new-wearer allowances exist only on fittings. J6: no exam-and-eyewear allowance on out-of-network reimbursement. J7: frequency is the base rule in every computation document, never a factor. J8: no tier exists only on Exam Plus except the children's frame tier for plans without a frame benefit, which the coordinator admitted where it changes the number (on Exam Plus a child's out-of-network frame would otherwise get oon_child_frame_reimbursement).
SPLIT OF THE TWO MEMBER-CLAIM RULES (round 14, KB audit S1): one shared sentence, word for word the same in both rules and computed the same way in both, fixes the side by receipts alone: a claim whose spectacle-lens and frame retail charges together are at least its contact-lens and fitting retail charges together is settled on its glasses part, any other on its contact-lens part; each rule records nothing (0.00) for a claim of the other side and each member tool refuses such a claim, so exactly one rule claims every claim, whatever either rule's amounts. Inside its rule each claim keeps its in-lieu comparison of reimbursed parts at that rule's amounts.
DEPARTURES AND WHY: (1) Rounds 8-9 (K3, L1): the backup glasses' lens-type schedule cannot change the contact-lens claim's number while its contact-lens part is kept (its baseline oon_single_vision_reimbursement is the smallest lens amount), and the refit's tie needs that part kept; a ladder on the certified reason alone has only two values on the plans that carry a contacts benefit (contact_lens_reason is elective or medically_necessary; every plan with a contacts benefit has covered_in_full), and the plan tier for plans without a contacts benefit only selected 0.00 where every other tier is also 0.00 (Exam Plus). Round 9 takes the coordinator's option (a): the claim's in-lieu factor is a genuine three-tier method (a contact-lens service already counted in the benefit period leaves the glasses lines out; a claim with both parts pays the larger; a claim with contact lenses only pays every line), and the test of a spectacle-lens or frame service already counted in the period moves into a contact-lens amount factor, contacts_basis (parameter), with the tiers of the contact-lens order's in_lieu_basis (glasses already counted -> 0.00, the contact-lens line denied in lieu and its fitting following it; otherwise medically necessary -> oon_contacts_medically_necessary_reimbursement; otherwise elective -> oon_contacts_elective_reimbursement). Both factors read the period through the shared latest-service reads; neither reads the other's binding; the comparison and the order (contact-lens settlement first, then contacts-in-lieu) live in the assembly. A plan without a contacts benefit is handled by the claim rule's not-covered sentence (base vision_evt_in_network_benefits / vision_evt_medically_necessary_contacts), never by a factor tier. Options (b) and (c) were not taken: (b) leaves a two-value reason ladder, (c) would re-split the two member-claim rules and move task 0's glasses claim. (1b) Round 8 (K4): the compute language has no date-range aggregate, so a count of every paid service between two reset days cannot be computed exactly for every frozen date; the in-lieu test therefore reads the latest paid or reimbursed service of each kind of the other side, the way vision_msr_last_paid_service and base vision_evt_frequency count contact lenses against the lens and frame benefits, and counts it only in the service's own benefit period from the reset day. (2) The exam visit uses the copay band instead of the evaluation add-on: the add-on is excluded whenever the visit itself bills a fitting (H8 non-duplication), and the visit's fitting is what makes the exam-type fee schedule bite. (3) The decision tools book the claim's one amount on its first undenied line, the other lines carrying no separate amount, because the schema has no claim-level amount field.
TRIGGER RULE (XF-14): tools write only vision_claims rows of vision_exam_claim, vision_lens_claim, vision_frame_claim and vision_contacts_claim; base triggers [] for all four.
FACTOR INDEPENDENCE (XF-1, round 8 re-run): scratch checks8.py closes every factor binding's reads through plain bindings; no factor reaches another factor's binding, no plain binding other than result reads a factor binding, no duplicate binding names: "checks bad = 0".
QUOTE SWEEP (XF-9): every compute_basis value, policy_source and replaced_by is a verbatim substring of its rule (0 misses); each rounding sentence matches the single int(x*100+0.5)/100 around result.
METHOD-SHAPE ALL-PAIRS: eligibility_binder (all six): late (constant) vs binder (benefit formula) vs record (status/date pick) - each pair differs by an operation or input. in-lieu (glasses claim): drop contact side vs drop glasses side vs keep the larger (adds a comparison) vs keep all (adds both sides). in-lieu (contact-lens claim): drop glasses side vs keep the larger (adds a comparison) vs keep all. user_scenario: You are Helena Marsh, a dental hygienist in Tacoma who is new to Cascade Mutual: in November you signed yourself and your sixteen-year-old daughter Ivy up for Cascade Vision Select 150, starting December 1, and the check you mailed for the first premium was booked on December 28.
